subject: ACME: follow-up — competitive incident response & next tests
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME: follow-up — competitive incident response & next tests

Hi John / Samantha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) What we heard from ACME:
- Primary concerns: incident detection & response SLAs, RCA turnaround time, and escalation paths for production degradations.
- You want structured evidence comparing Redwood vs the hyperscalers and other inference API vendors on support SLAs and RCA commitments.

2) What Redwood will deliver
- A short incident-response comparison doc (attached) summarizing SLA tiers, escalation matrices, and typical RCA windows for Redwood, AWS SageMaker endpoints, GCP Vertex AI, and OpenAI/other API providers.
- Proposal for the next technical test: a simulated degraded-throughput scenario (controlled prefix-heavy workload) to validate fallback behavior, latency degradation profile, and end-to-end alerting/notifications.

3) Ask from ACME (confirm):
- Which SLA targets matter most (P99 latency, time-to-detect, time-to-RCA, time-to-fix)?
- Do you need vendor-signed RCAs or is an engineer-led postmortem acceptable?
- Preferred window for the test next week (Mon/Tue preferred).

Next steps / timeline:
- I’ll attach the Incident_Response_Comparison.pdf and a proposed MAA (mutual action plan) draft (MAA-proposal-v1.pdf).
- If that looks good, we’ll schedule the simulated run and loop in Marissa for the SLA escalation discussion.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call to walk through the doc.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME: follow-up — competitive incident response & next tests

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A couple of clarifications: 

- SLA priorities: Time-to-detect and Time-to-RCA are top (we want detection within 5 mins and an initial RCA summary within 24 hours for Sev-1). P99 latency SLOs are also important but secondary.
- Vendor-signed RCAs: for now we prefer vendor-signed high-level RCAs for Sev-1 incidents (legal will need to see a formal statement). Engineer-led postmortems are fine for lower severities.

About the test: Tue 23rd morning PST works for us (we have a change window). Can you confirm scope (will the test require any data ingress/egress, or is it purely load simulation)? Also curious if you can include an apples-to-apples latency degradation graph versus GCP/AWS — even if simulated.

John
Sr. Director, Platform Engineering | ACME Corp
john.doe@acme.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME: follow-up — competitive incident response & next tests

John — great, thanks for the priorities. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

- Detection & RCA targets: We typically commit to 5–15 min detection for platform-detected Sev-1 and provide an initial RCA summary within 24 hours. For enterprise Dedicated customers we can contract tighter RCAs (including vendor-signed PDFs) in the enterprise addendum. See section 2 of the attached Incident_Response_Comparison.pdf for details.

- Test scope: the proposed simulation will be a load test that exercises prefix-heavy, long-context workloads to surface KV cache and routing fallbacks. It is purely synthetic — no customer data required. We’ll run from our dedicated test harness and provide logs and timeline artifacts; we can also run a parallel run on a public hyperscaler instance (synthetic) to produce an apples-to-apples latency comparison.

- Deliverables: post-test we’ll provide
  * timeline of detection/alerting
  * P50/P95/P99 latency curves across the run
  * timeline of any fallbacks and their triggers
  * initial RCA (within 24 hours) and fuller RCA within 72 hours if the issue is non-trivial

- Tue 23rd morning PST works for Redwood. I’ll lock in the window if that works for you.

Proposed next action: Confirm Tue 23rd 09:00–10:30 PST. I’ll send calendar invite and the test plan.

Thanks,
Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME: follow-up — competitive incident response & next tests

John / team — adding a couple of operational notes from our side. Attaching the brief comparison PDF. Highlights: 

- Hyperscalers (AWS/GCP): typically rely on shared control planes for managed endpoints; detection is fast but vendor RCAs vary — some provide engineering-signed RCAs only on escalations / enterprise contracts. Latency degradation during regional issues often tied to cold-start and autoscaling behavior.

- OpenAPI-style providers: variable SLA language; many are reactive (post-incident summaries) and do not offer SLA-backed remedies for model-level hallucinations or inference quality regressions.

- Redwood differentiators:
  * Dedicated pools option with SLA-backed detection & response windows for reserved capacity customers
  * Explicit escalation matrix (L1 support → Engineering on-call → Customer Success → Executive escalation) included in enterprise contracts
  * We provide artifacted RCAs (PDFs) for Sev-1 under enterprise addendum and maintain an incident portal for timeline visibility

Attached: Incident_Response_Comparison.pdf (one-page comparison) and MAA-proposal-v1.pdf (draft timeline / decision points). Happy to revise the MAA after your feedback.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME: follow-up — competitive incident response & next tests

Thanks Rishi / Marissa — the comparison looks useful and confirms a few of our assumptions. We’re in agreement to proceed with the Tue 23rd 09:00–10:30 PST window. A couple of final asks before the run: 

- Please include a one-page executive summary of what the vendor-signed RCA would look like (we’ll drop that into our legal packet).
- Add the expected timeline for a formal signed RCA (we prefer a single PDF signed and dated within 5 business days for Sev-1).

If you can put those two items into the MAA and send an updated doc by EOD today, we’ll accept the test window and I’ll send the change-window confirmation.

John
